config.qb1_selection: decision #36 (2026-09-24): scripts/make_report.py overrides star_pool's usage-ranked QB1 with the sportsbook's own pick when FanDuel prices passing_yards for exactly one QB on a team. Applies only to QB; RB/WR/TE picks are untouched. Does not change project.py's projection math or the passing_yards calibration/config above -- only which player's row gets shown as QB1.
config.decision_37: 2026-09-24: (1) fetch_lines()/event_lines() now save the raw Odds API response to data/boards/ before any filtering, zero extra API calls. (2) nflprops/report.py's build()/render() -- the code path the scheduled launchd jobs actually run via scripts/run_reports.py -- brought to parity with scripts/make_report.py: it previously had NEITHER decision #31's phase3 merge NOR decision #36's QB1 override, so neither had ever reached a scheduled report before this fix. (3) templates/report.html shows project.py and Phase 3 side by side with the gap, emphasized when it exceeds half the card's own spread; presentation only, no prediction math changed.

passing_yards.train_seasons: rolling -- every REG-season game strictly before the predicted week, no fixed cutoff (nflprops/project.py:_history)

informational_only.phase3_engine: ridge, scripts/retrain_vol_models.py -> data/shipping/passing_yards.pkl (decision #39, 2026-09-24). Trained on features.db's QB passing features (pass_attempts/completions/yards_per_attempt/completion_rate/pass_adot, l4/l8/career) added the same day, plus the shared usage/context feature set. build_design(..., include_passing=True) is required to serve or refit this artifact -- the default (False) excludes those columns so the other four vol/yardage models' design matrices stay exactly as they were before #39 (see rung2_ridge.PASSING_COLS).
informational_only.head_to_head_result: ridge wins, +6.76% MAE lift over project.py, 5/5 seasons (decision #39, scripts/passing_head_to_head.py, 2021-2025 walk-forward, n=3,107; project.py 67.09 MAE vs ridge 62.56 MAE). Shipped additively per decision #37's posture regardless -- shown as a second number on the card, never replacing project.py's own.

known_open_bug_before_holdout.description: nflprops.project._roster() showed Tua Tagovailoa on ATL for 2026 W3. Decision #31 flagged this as a suspected data bug (assumed MIA); decision #34 'fixed' it as a data correction to MIA. Decision #35 (2026-09-24) reverted #34: Sean confirmed Tua genuinely moved to Atlanta in 2026. The upstream nflreadpy roster value was correct all along -- there was never a roster-pipeline bug. _roster(), ingest.py's team-mapping, and the rosters table all reflect ATL, which is right.
known_open_bug_before_holdout.status: closed, decision #35 (2026-09-24) -- false positive, no bug existed. The real risk this surfaced was in nflprops/reliability.py's star_pool(): a player who switches teams and hasn't played yet can still outrank the actual current starter, because usage was ranked on career history regardless of how stale it is. Fixed generally in decision #35 -- star_pool() now zeroes usage for any player flagged changed_team by role_continuity() who also has zero games this season, so an unconfirmed role can't outrank someone actually on the field. reliability.py is not in this manifest's code_sha256 (it sits outside the locked engine, same as ingest.py), so the engine lock and this file's hashes are unaffected; engine/check_drift.py still passes.
